<DIV align="center" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>Vale &#151; 2010 Production Report</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>A YEAR OF STRONG RECOVERY</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Rio de Janeiro, February&nbsp;24, 2011 &#151; Vale S.A. (Vale) operations had an outstanding
performance in 2010. After facing the challenges stemming from the global recession of 2008/2009,
one of the deepest in modern economic history, there was a strong recovery of the output of most of
our products.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The production of iron ore of 308 Mt<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">1</SUP> in 2010 achieved an all-time high figure. It was
29.4% above 2009 and 1.5% higher than the previous record level of 303 Mt attained in 2007, a year
of fast global demand growth and full capacity operation. Caraj&#225;s, which has the best iron ore
deposits in the world, produced 101 Mt in this year, establishing a new record mark. At the same
time, pellet production was 49 Mt, another all-time figure, surpassing the previous record of 45 Mt
of 2007. In addition, new records were reached in the production of bauxite, at 14 Mt, and coal,
6.9 Mt.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The bulk of our Canadian nickel operations, encompassing the Sudbury and Voisey Bay sites, were
negatively affected by a long strike, which started in 3Q09. Despite the labor interruption, we
managed to keep the operations running, albeit at low levels of capacity utilization. With the end
of the strike in Sudbury, the output of refined nickel began to increase in 3Q10 and in the last
quarter of the year climbed to an annualized rate of 260,000 metric tons, an almost normal level of
activity, even higher than the production number for 2007, of 248,000 metric tons.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The move towards normalization of our base metals production and its minor and precious metals
by-products is taking place against a backdrop of high and rising prices, contributing to a
significant enhancement of our financial performance.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In the first weeks of this year there were heavy rains and flooding in some parts of Brazil &#151;
where we have 100% of our iron ore operations &#151; and in the state of Queensland, Australia &#151; where
our central Australian office, in Brisbane, and some of our coal mines are located. Although the
rainfall was far heavier than the seasonal standard, the preemptive actions taken by our bulk
materials operations were able to minimize output losses.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In the case of iron ore, so far losses have been minimal, estimated to reach only 600,000 metric
tons (200,000 in the Southern System and 400,000 in the Southeastern System), which are in
accordance with the seasonality pattern for the first quarter of each year and represent only a
minimal portion of the total production target for 2011, 311 Mt<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">2</SUP>, thus being easily
recoverable over the year. On the other hand, the estimated losses for our coal production in
Queensland, at 500,000 metric tons, are relevant given the still small scale of Vale&#146;s Australian
operations.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Given the strong global demand for minerals and metals and the positive expectations for the near
term, the excellence of our current operations and the upcoming capacity additions from soon to be
delivered new projects, as well as those which are already being commissioned and ramped up, we
expect the continuation of the outstanding operational performance and a significant contribution
to shareholder value creation.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>BULK MATERIALS</B>

    <TD align="right">3.0</TD>
    <TD nowrap>%</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD align="right">25.4</TD>
    <TD nowrap>%</TD>
</TR>
<!-- End Table Body -->
</TABLE>
</DIV>



<DIV align="left">
<DIV style="font-size: 3pt; margin-top: 3pt; width: 18%; border-top: 0px solid #000000">&nbsp;</DIV>
</DIV>

<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">
<TR style="font-size: 6pt">
    <TD width="3%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="96%">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left"><SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">1</SUP></TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">Vale&#146;s attributable production capacity of 50%.</DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>



<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Vale&#146;s iron ore production reached a new record in 2010, namely 307.8 Mt, with a
year-over-year increase of 29.4%, thus surpassing the 2007 record of 303.2 Mt.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Production was 80.3 Mt in 4Q10, 2.8% below 3Q10, which in light of seasonality is a very slight
decrease (4Q of each year tends to have a lower production than 3Q due to the beginning of the
rainy season in the last months of the year, while the third quarter is the seasonally strongest
quarter of the year for iron ore production).
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Following its recovery in 3Q10, iron ore production in Caraj&#225;s reached 28 Mt in 4Q10, expanding by
3.7% on a quarter-on-quarter basis and 33.7% year-on-year. Given its outstanding
performance in the second half of the year, the 2010 output level of 101.2 Mt surpassed the
previous record for Caraj&#225;s, achieved in 2008, at 96.5 Mt.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The Southeastern System, which encompasses the Itabira, Mariana and Minas Centrais mining sites,
reached a production of 30.0 Mt, decreasing 4.8% over 3Q10 due to seasonal factors and rising 22.3%
over 4Q09.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The Southern System produced 18.2 Mt in 4Q10 against 20.2Mt in 3Q10, but increased 24.8% on a
year-on-year basis.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Our iron ore mines, Urucum and Corumb&#225;, located in state of Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, near the
border with Bolivia and Paraguay, were aggregated under the newly created Midwestern System. It is
the smallest of our Systems, with a production of 1.3 Mt in 4Q10 and a quarter-on-quarter increase
of 16.5% and 85.6% year-on-year.
</DIV>

    <TD nowrap align="left"><SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">2</SUP></TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">Vale&#146;s attributable production capacity of 50%.</DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>



<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 4Q10, pellet production was 12.2 Mt, 10.5% lower than the previous quarter but 39.5%
higher than 4Q09. The total volume produced in 2010 reached 49 Mt &#151; a new all-time high, 9.3%
higher than the 44.8 Mt record achieved in 2007.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">There were some scheduled maintenance stoppages in 4Q10, which affected negatively output
performance. The plants were under maintenance in October, S&#227;o Luis in November, and Tubar&#227;o I and
II in December while some Hispanobr&#225;s equipment was under maintenance during November.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Vargem Grande also had some operational issues, arising from the supply and quality of feed
received.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The three pellet plants of the 50%-owned Samarco JV, which have a nominal capacity of 21.0 Mtpy,
were operating at full capacity. Our attributable production was 2,833 Mt in 4Q10, 2.2% lower than
3Q10.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The Oman operations, in the industrial site of Sohar, Oman, are coming on stream. It has two
pellets plants, each with a capacity to produce 4.5 Mtpy, thus adding 9.0 Mtpy to our production
capacity. The two plants will produce direct reduction pellets.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Oman&#146;s plant 1 is under commissioning and furnace heating, and is expected to start up production
in March. Plant 2 is being assembled and is expected to reach the ramp up stage by the end of the
first half of this year.
</DIV>


<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->3<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 4Q10, manganese ore production was slightly higher than the previous quarter, coming
to 477,000 t against 472,000 t in 3Q10. The annual output increased 11.1% when compared to 2009,
reaching 1.8 Mt.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The production of Azul &#151; our largest manganese mine &#151; increased 5.1% on a quarter-on-quarter
basis, reaching 391,000t. The use of new equipment has contributed to improve mining performance.
The total production in 2010 was 12.1% above 2009.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Ferroalloy quarterly production was comprised of 51,000t of ferrosilicon manganese alloys (FeSiMn),
60,000t of high-carbon manganese alloys (FeMnHc) and 5,000 t of medium-carbon manganese alloys
(FeMnMC). The total output was slightly higher than previous quarter, increasing by 3.8%.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Production for 2010 was 451,000t, more than doubling relatively to 2009, but still lower than the
previous peak of 542,000t reached in 2007.
</DIV>


<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->4<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Despite the adverse weather conditions in Australia and some operational issues, 2010
was our best year for coal operations, with all-time high levels of production for both
metallurgical and thermal coal, 3.057 Mt and 3.832 Mt, respectively, totaling 6.9 Mt.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 4Q10 Vale&#146;s coal production reached 1.75 Mt, which was comprised of 770,000 t of metallurgical
coal and 976,000 t of thermal coal.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Production of metallurgical and thermal coal at Integra Coal, in New South Wales, was 279,000 t and
74,000t, respectively, in 4Q10. Both metallurgical and thermal coal output were lower than in 3Q10.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Production at Carborough Downs, in Queensland, was 367,000 t in 4Q10, versus 289,000 t in 3Q10.
Although Carborough Downs completed a long wall move in 4Q10, the increase in its yield on this
quarter contributed to a higher output and its best ever quarterly performance.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Heavy and consistent rainfall during the fourth quarter resulted in 42&nbsp;days of lost production at
all other mines in the state of Queensland.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The thermal coal mine of El Hatillo, an open pit coal mine in Colombia, is ramping up and was also
affected by bad weather conditions in the 4Q10 producing 830,000 t in 4Q10, in line with 3Q10.
</DIV>


<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->5<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<DIV align="left">
<DIV style="font-size: 3pt; margin-top: 3pt; width: 18%; border-top: 0px solid #000000">&nbsp;</DIV>
</DIV>

<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">
<TR style="font-size: 6pt">
    <TD width="3%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="96%">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left">*</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><DIV style="text-align: justify">External feed purchased from third parties and processed into finished nickel in our operations</DIV></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>



<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Total finished nickel production was 65,000 t in 4Q10, 45.7% up on a quarter-on-quarter
basis, being our highest quarterly output since 1Q09. Most of this increase &#151; about 15,000 t &#151; was
due to the significant contribution of Voisey Bay feed to refined nickel.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Voisey Bay mining and processing has been operating at full capacity for some time focusing on high
grade feed to supply the Clydach and Thompson refineries. At the same time, Sudbury mining was more
focused on high grade copper and was operating at levels much below capacity. Mining was ramped up
only after the end of the strike and given the relatively long production cycle, from mined nickel
to refined nickel, the fourth quarter still saw the numbers for refined nickel sourced from Sudbury
at low levels, increasing to only 8,000 t from 6,000 t in 3Q10.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">During 1H11, one of the two furnaces of our Copper Cliff smelter in Sudbury will remain shutdown
for a minimum of 16&nbsp;weeks, entailing an estimated output loss of 15,000 metric tons of finished
nickel.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Production at Thompson in 4Q10 was 8,300 t, 75.2% up from the previous quarter as the operations
had a one-month annual maintenance shutdown in 3Q10.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Finished nickel production sourced from Sorowako, Indonesia, was 19,600 t, down 9.7% from 3Q10 due
to a maintenance shutdown in October at the Matsuzaka refinery in Japan. It was up 34.7% on a
year-on-year basis as at 4Q09 the Sorowako matte was being diverted to the Clydach refinery to meet
demand requirements which contributed to lengthen the production cycle at that time.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The commissioning of the On&#231;a Puma ferronickel project is completed, with the production of the
first metal was in the last week of January. The operation has a nominal production capacity of
58,000 t of nickel in ferronickel.
</DIV>



<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->6<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

</TABLE>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Vale&#146;s copper production was 76,000t in 4Q10, an increase of 30.3% on a
quarter-on-quarter basis.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Production of copper in concentrates from the Sossego mine at Caraj&#225;s was 6% lower than in the
previous quarter due to the smaller volumes of feed received by the plant during this quarter.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Our Canadian operations delivered 46,000 t in 4Q10, 20,000t higher than 3Q10. In addition to the
better performance of Voisey&#146;s Bay, there was a contribution of copper ores purchased from third
parties in previous quarters and processed into copper concentrates and anodes in Sudbury in 4Q10.
These purchases allowed us to increase copper shipments in an environment of rising prices.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Similarly to nickel, there was a sharp increase in the production of cobalt, platinum
group metals and precious metals in 4Q10.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Cobalt production in 4Q10 was 624,000 t, up 491,000 t from 3Q10 due to the ramping up of operations
in Sudbury after the end of the labor interruption.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Production of platinum and palladium in 4Q10 was 61,000 troy ounces, which was 51,000 troy ounces
higher than in 3Q10 and 55,000 troy ounces higher than 4Q09.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Our production of bauxite in 2010 achieved an all-time high at 14.332 Mt, showing a
significant growth against the mark 12.461 Mt in 2009. Due to the conclusion and further expansion
of the Paragominas mining operations our bauxite production has more than doubled over the last
five years, coming from 6.884 Mt in 2005 to 14.332 Mt in 2010.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">A record quarterly output was reached in 4Q10, when Vale&#146;s bauxite production totaled 3.851 Mt,
1.3% higher on a quarter-on-quarter basis and 15% year-on-year.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Vale&#146;s production at Trombetas was slightly lower than during the previous quarter. But, on the
other hand, Paragominas output reached an all-time high production of 2.0 Mt, 5.2% higher than
3Q10.
</DIV>

    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD align="right">169</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD align="right">717</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>

    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>

    <TD align="right">9.0</TD>
    <TD nowrap>%</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD nowrap align="right">-8.8</TD>
    <TD nowrap>%</TD>

    <TD nowrap align="left">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD nowrap align="right">-7.6</TD>
    <TD nowrap>%</TD>

</TABLE>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In 4Q10, production of potash was 169,000 t, a volume 14,000 t higher than 3Q10. The
rise in output is explained by an improvement in asset utilization in mining.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Vale Fosfatados owns two phosphate rock mines, Arax&#225;, in the state of Minas Gerais, and Cajati, in the state of S&#227;o Paulo, Brazil.
Alongside the mining operations, the assets also comprise four processing plants for the production of phosphates fertilizers
located at: (a)&nbsp;Arax&#225;, state of Minas Gerais; (b)&nbsp;Cajati, state of S&#227;o Paulo; (c)&nbsp;Cubat&#227;o, state of S&#227;o Paulo; (d)&nbsp;Guar&#225;, state of
S&#227;o Paulo.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Total production of phosphate rock, which is used to feed the output of phosphate
nutrients, rose 49.1% compared to 3Q10. Vale Fertilizantes and Vale Fosfatados had an output
performance in line with 3Q10. Bay&#243;var, our Peruvian phosphate rock mine, started to ramp up
production in July and produced 582,000 metric tons in 4Q10.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The production of MAP (monoammonium phosphate) was 245,000 t, up 7.1% quarter-on-quarter, in
response to the stronger demand in the Brazilian market.
</DIV>

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->9<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">TSP (triple superphosphate) production decreased 29.4% compared to 3Q10, due to a maintenance
stoppage in 4Q10.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The production of SSP (single superphosphate) from Vale Fosfatados reduced 14.5% from 3Q10 due to
the maintenance stoppage in the Cubat&#227;o plant. Production of Vale Fertilizantes was 18.1% lower
than in previous quarter due to a maintenance stoppage at the Catal&#227;o plant.
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">DCP (dicalcium phosphate) decreased by 29.8% on a quarter-on-quarter basis due to a maintenance
stoppage at the Arauc&#225;ria plant.
</DIV>
